articles.description: Elon Musk’s $1 trillion SpaceX prediction is probably wrong. Contrarian investors are buying these out-of-favor value plays instead.

analysis.summary: Wall Street investors are increasingly interested in undervalued stocks and contrarian value plays rather than high-growth stocks. The article examines 10 out-of-favor stocks that contrarian investors believe are positioned to perform well, while questioning the feasibility of Elon Musk's $1 trillion valuation prediction for SpaceX.

articles.title: Stock investors expect the Fed to save them. But no ‘Warsh put’ is coming.
articles.description: Wall Street’s belief in a central bank safety net misreads the dot-com crash. Alan Greenspan was following rules — not saving portfolios.

analysis.summary: Stock investors are betting on Federal Reserve intervention to support markets, but analysts argue this expectation misinterprets historical precedent. The article examines how Fed Chair Alan Greenspan's actions during the dot-com crash followed monetary policy rules rather than intentionally protecting investor portfolios, suggesting current market confidence in a potential "Warsh put" may be unfounded.

articles.description: Young Chinese aren’t buying status symbols. They’re spending money on things that make them feel something — anything.

analysis.summary: Young Chinese consumers are shifting spending patterns away from traditional status symbols toward products that provide emotional satisfaction, including toy elves and robotic products. This trend reflects changing consumer priorities among China's youth toward experiential and emotional value rather than material status.
